("Chorus") (CHR) today announced its third quarter 2026 financial results."Our strong performance gives us the confidence to raise our 2026 guidance, while the acquisition of SkyCare accelerates the growth and diversification of Chorus. The transformation of Chorus is gaining momentum. With SkyCare now part of the platform, alongside continued growth at Voyageur and KADEX, we expect revenue from parts sales, contract flying, MRO, and other to reach $265.0 million to $300.0 million in 2027, approximately double 2025 levels. This represents a meaningful increase in the scale of our businesses outside of the CPA and further advances our strategy to build a more diversified aviation, aerospace and defence platform," said Colin Copp, President and Chief Executive Officer of Chorus."The addition of SkyCare is an exciting milestone for Chorus and another meaningful step in the continued growth of our platform. SkyCare brings specialized aviation and medical capabilities, strong customer relationships and an experienced team. We are very pleased to welcome Frank Behrendt and the entire team to Chorus and look forward to supporting SkyCare's continued success and identifying new opportunities, including those across our businesses."Q3 2026 Financial Highlights(unaudited)(expressed in thousands of Canadian dollars)Three months ended September 30,Nine months ended September 30,20262025ChangeChange20262025ChangeChange$$$%$$$%Operating revenue346,128323,56722,5617.01,020,972996,30824,6642.5Operating expenses323,788298,72025,0688.4955,605917,67937,9264.1Operating income22,34024,847(2,507)(10.1)65,36778,629(13,262)(16.9)Net interest expense(2,720)(3,151)43113.7(9,160)(10,404)1,24412.0Foreign exchange gain (loss)543(5,213)5,756110.4(7,913)7,200(15,113)209.9Gain on property and equipment2,220—2,220100.04,695104,68546,850.0Income before income tax22,38316,4835,90035.852,98975,435(22,446)(29.8)Income tax expense(6,735)(5,817)(918)(15.8)(16,516)(13,399)(3,117)(23.3)Net income15,64810,6664,98246.736,47362,036(25,563)(41.2)Adjusted EBITDA(1)47,69151,569(3,878)(7.5)142,742159,759(17,017)(10.7)Adjusted EBT(1)21,96621,1827843.763,74661,3552,3913.9Adjusted Net Income(1)15,12415,365(241)(1.6)46,81344,8082,0054.5(1)These are non-GAAP financial measures that are not recognized measures for financial statement presentation under GAAP. anda negative change in income tax, including tax on adjusted items of $2.7 million; partially offset bythe previously noted increase in Adjusted Net Income of $2.0 million.Completed SkyCare AcquisitionOn November 1, 2026, Chorus completed the acquisition of SkyCare Air Ambulance ("SkyCare"), a provider of aviation and medical services headquartered in Sioux Lookout, Ontario, for a purchase price of approximately $40.0 million. At closing, Chorus funded $36.1 million through the Operating Credit Facility and cash on hand inclusive of an estimated net working capital adjustment of $4.1 million. The remaining purchase price is subject to customary adjustments and includes contingent consideration dependent on SkyCare's achievement of certain future performance targets, payable through to March 31, 2029. The transaction advances Chorus' strategy of building a broader aviation, aerospace and defence operating platform through the addition of specialized capabilities, complementary operations and long-standing customer relationships. Chorus expects the acquisition to be immediately accretive to its earnings and Free Cash Flow and to generate investment returns in the mid-teens.Progressed Aircraft SalesIn 2025, Chorus executed agreements to sell nine Dash 8-400s as they exit the fleet in accordance with the CPA, subject to customary closing conditions and the completion of contractual maintenance events for estimated net proceeds of US $62.0 million. Eight aircraft have been sold to-date (seven in 2026 and one in Q4 2025), one of which was sold in the third quarter of 2026 resulting in a gain on sale of CAD $2.2 million. The remaining aircraft is expected to close by December 2026, subject to customary closing conditions as well as the completion of contractual maintenance events, with net proceeds of approximately US $7.4 million.Continued Share RepurchasesOn February 12, 2026, the Corporation announced the renewal of its normal course issuer bid ("NCIB"). Under the NCIB, the Corporation is authorized to purchase for cancellation up to a maximum of 1,963,003 of its Common Shares. During the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Corporation purchased and cancelled 615,402 Common Shares under the NCIB at a weighted average price of $27.27 per Common Share for $16.8 million. During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Corporation purchased and cancelled 1,460,378 Common Shares under the NCIB at a weighted average price of $25.21 per Common Share for $36.8 million.Dividend DeclarationThe Board of Directors of Chorus today declared a cash dividend of $0.11 per Class A Variable Voting Share and Class B Voting Share payable on December 29, 2026 to Shareholders of record at the close of business on December 14, 2026.This dividend is an eligible dividend in Canada. It may also be considered a qualified dividend from a U.S. tax perspective; however, shareholders should consult their tax advisor to confirm the treatment of the dividend under U.S. tax laws.Outlook1Chorus expects its revenue from parts sales, contract flying, MRO and other to be between $200.0 million and $220.0 million in 2026 and $265.0 million and $300.0 million in 2027.
